A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoMaGen work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulation experiments on demonstration generation and policy learning, plus real-robot results in Section 5.4 and Appendix A.1.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds failure distributions, component timing measurements, and qualitative demonstrations on additional tasks.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4, Algorithm 1, and Appendix C retain the same generation pipeline, constraints, and policy architectures. The newly disclosed sampling detail and additional applications do not document a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds Pour Cat Food, involving rigid-particle transfer, and Push Chair, requiring coupled base movement and sustained end-effector contact. These substantially broaden task requirements beyond the retained benchmarks and Get Bottle example, although the additions are qualitative demonstrations rather than quantified benchmark evaluations.

E2.justification: SkillMimicGen and DexMimicGen remain the evaluated baselines in Tables 2–3 and Figure 6. Visibility-ablation variants and sim-to-real controls are also unchanged. The removed SafeMimic citation was not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: V2 adds failure-cause and task-step attribution and component wall-clock profiling. Figure 10 computes average component duration shares only over successful episodes. Existing randomization schemes, training splits, policy-evaluation episode counts, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained visibility ablations, diversity analyses, and scaling study, Section 5.5 adds failure-cause breakdowns across D0–D2 and component runtime analyses. Appendix B.6 adds failure distributions across individual task steps. These substantially expand diagnosis of reliability and computational bottlenecks.

E5.justification: The new component-timing plot in Figure 9 introduces error bars and accompanying discussion of timing variance. Their statistical meaning and sample counts are unspecified. Neither additional training seeds nor increased repeated-run counts are established.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and policy results remain unchanged. V2 adds substantial diagnostic results, including approximately 35% of failures attributed to simulation instabilities, approximately 18 seconds for base planning versus 100 seconds for execution, and task-step failure distributions. Appendix B.1 also reports successful new task behaviors qualitatively. These are added findings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, trajectory transformations, and constrained optimization in Equation 1 are unchanged. No new or revised formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about constrained demonstration generation, diversity and visibility, learning from one source demonstration, and real-world deployment after limited fine-tuning. The additional evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 newly explains navigation failures through floor obstacles and sampling variability through sparse feasible base poses, suggesting controller, simulator, and sampling improvements. Appendix B.1 broadens the applicability discussion to pouring and whole-body coordination, but Section 6 still states that only alternating navigation and manipulation are demonstrated.

D1.justification: Section 5.5 newly describes sampling within a ring-shaped region and reports component-level runtimes. The reproducibility statement adds reported website access to code and reproduction instructions, previously described through the supplementary submission. Existing hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 removes the human-video imitation clause citing SafeMimic, together with the Bahety et al. reference. The remaining related-work discussion and positioning against prior demonstration-generation approaches are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds Section 5.5 and Appendix B.6, retitles and restructures B.1 around three task families, makes small wording corrections, and adds the ICLR 2026 publication header. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 8–10 and 16 introduce a substantial suite of diagnostic displays: failure-cause pies, component timing bars, runtime-share pies, and task-step failure pies. Existing figures and tables are preserved, with renumbering and appendix rearrangement that places some visuals alongside their associated text.

improvement.justification: V1 supplied aggregate performance evidence and a coarse compute-cost range; v2 adds useful explanations and measurements of failure sources and runtime bottlenecks, improving diagnostic transparency. The gains are bounded by qualitative-only new task examples, undefined timing error bars, and the inconsistency between B.1's whole-body demonstration and Section 6's unchanged limitation. The established comparative evidence remains intact.
